TECHNICAL DRAWINGS - REPRESENTATION OF SPLINES AND SERRATIONS
NATIONAL FOREWORD This Indian Standard, which is identical with IS0 6413 : 1988 `Technical drawings - Representation of splines and serrations' issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ), was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on the recommendations of the Drawing Sectional Committee ( LMD 02 ) and approval of the Light Mechanical Engineering Division Council. ln the adopted standard certain terminology and conventions are not identical with those used'in Indian Standards; attention is especially drawn to the following: a) Wherever the words `International Standard' appear reFerring to this standard, they should be read as `Indian Standard'. b) Comma ( , ) has been used as a decimal marker while practice is to use point ( . ) as the decimal marker. in Indian Standards'the current

In the adopted standard, reference appears to certain International Standards for which Indian Standards also exist. The corresponding Indian Standards which are to be substituted in their place are listed below along with their degree of equiva!ence for the edition indicated: International Standard IS0 14 : 1982 Indian Standard IS 2327 : 1963 Dimensions for straight sided splines for general engineering use IS 10714 : 1983 Geneial principles of presentation on technical drawings IS 9609 ( Part 1 ) : 1983 Lettering on technical drawings : Part 1 English characters Degree of Equivalence Identical

IS0 128 : 1982 IS0 3098 - 1 : 1974

Identical Identical

The concerned technical committee has reviewed the provisions of IS0 3461-2 : 1987 and IS0 4156 : 1981 referred in this addpted standard and has decided that they are acceptable for use in conjunction with this standard.

4.2

Method

for indicating

designation

Figure 5 shows an example of a complete representation of an involute spline joint.

The designation shoujd be indicated near the feature but always connected to the contour of the spline joint by a leader line (see figure 3).

Figure 3 Figure 5 Where a spline joint is not in accordance with a standard as mentioned above, or where the requirement is modified, the necessary data shall be tabulated on the drawing or any other associated document and shall be cross-referenced by aJeader line and grapnical symbol to the applicable contour. Figure, 6 shows an example of a complete representation of a serration.

5

Complete

representation

of spline

joints

A complete representation of spline joints showing all details with their true dimensions is generally not necessary in a technical drawing and should be avoided. If such a representation has to be made, the drawing rules laid down in IS0 126 shall be applied. If necessary, a designation of the spline joint in accordance with clause 4 may be added. Figure 4 shows an example of a complete representation of a straight-sided spline joint. Figure 6

6.2.2 6.2.1 Contours and edges

Root surface

For straight-sided splines, the root surface (minor diameter of external splined part, major diameter of internal spline) shall be drawn with a continuous thin line (see IS0 128, line type 6).

The contours and edges of a shaft (e.g. an external spline) or a hub (e.g. an internal spline) shall be drawn as if they were in an unsectioned view, solid parts (without teeth) bounded by a cylinder representing the tip surface (outside

-

In the axial section of a splined shaft or hub, however, the root surface shall be drawn with a continuous thick line (see IS0 128, line type A) in accordance with table 1.

IS 13088 IS0 6413

: 1988

6.2.3

Pitch surface

6.2.7

Detailed

drawing

of tooth profile

The pitch surface (pitch diameter) shall be drawn with a thin chain line (see IS0 128, line type G) for involute splines and serrations.

If the designation is not sufficiently clear, a detailed drawing of the tooth profile should be added (see figure 10).

6.2.4

Usable length

The usable length of the splined part shall be represented with a continuous thick line (see IS0 128, line type AJ (see figure 7). Usually, only the usable length of a splined part shall be drawn. Figure 10 6.2.6 Tool run-out

If necessary, the tool run-out may be represented by an oblique line or a radius with the same line as used for the root surface (see figures 7 and 8).

6.2.8

Surface texture

If it is necessary to specify the surface texture of the contacting surfaces (excluding root and tip diameter), the graphical symbol, the designation and the drawing indications used for surface texture should be indicated on a common leader line as shown in figure 11.
